issues.description: The frozen inventory contains two PDFs and three program files but no empirical datasets. Required routes, product versions, fields, identifiers, and histories remain unverified. Compatible author-prepared data are preferred alternatives where they can supply the required inputs.
The AAER program has a dynamic macros.sas include and unresolved macro/library context; that support file is absent from the assigned inventory, so expansion and output locations remain unknown.

The AAER SAS code names state/county JAR and highmedia/lowmedia PROC FREQ outputs and creates a Zipcode dataset from SASHELP.ZIPCODE, while HERI/EMSI read corresponding physical inputs. Persisting/copying each named product to the exact existing consumer paths is supported routing/setup preparation. Keep the CCM and EMSI roots distinct; this preparation does not declare their files identical.

The HERI major-label block reads the 2016 and 2020 OriginalsDTA disagg paths before later code creates those exact files. The label outputs are not used later in the supplied do-file, but the early reads can stop the file when no prior copy exists; this is a source-supported order-preparation candidate.

The .sas container includes SAS imports/transforms and an explicit Stata regression block after PROC EXPORT. Assess both supplied segments; extraction/routing at that boundary is preparation, and the extension alone does not establish the language of the whole file.

The SAS segment constructs dataset all from bachelors15c and exports it as Stata format immediately before the explicit Stata regression block. Adding a Stata load for this preceding export and routing the block into a driver are known setup preparation steps. Preserve the supplied model and sample; validate the exported fields and configured path before any future run.

The named producer/consumer stages do not establish data-level compatibility for every state/county JAR, highmedia, lowmedia and ZIP product: exact fields, variant definitions and historical coverage still require validation at each consumer. Distinct roots and similar basenames do not prove equivalence.

actions.description: Prefer a compatible author-prepared fraud output. If raw AAER reconstruction is intended, resolve the missing macro context and source maps, and retain the exact named output variants for the supported persistence step. Confirm existing permitted access separately without conducting searches or inferring a missing license.
steps: Ask for complete author-prepared state/year and county/year JAR/highmedia/lowmedia inputs first, including identifiers, years, fields and media definitions.

If the raw route is needed, obtain the exact macros.sas include, AAER/LM/manual input files, and the author's Compustat/CRSP alias definitions; do not perform Factiva, company, person, or entity searches.
Confirm the user's current permitted access separately for any Factiva, Compustat, CRSP/WRDS or EMSI product; product names and the quoted author agreement do not prove the user's access status.
Confirm the existing SAS runtime and PC Files Server/EXCELCS configuration; do not assume availability from the installed-path listing.
validation: Before a future authorized run, verify the selected prepared or raw route has the exact consumed identifier fields and required period.
Map each generated product and variant to the exact named consumer input path; roots may differ, and field/history compatibility is validated separately.

actions.description: Request a compatible author-prepared HERI panel and covariates first. If raw inputs are intended, identify the exact 2016/2020 versions and missing maps/controls, then verify merge keys and years. Resolve the disagg read order before any future run.
steps: Use a complete author-prepared panel if its fields, sample years, identifiers and weights match the supplied consumer; do not require it in addition to raw files.
Otherwise obtain the named 2016 DTA and 2020 SAV source components plus the exact StateNamesAbbrev, HERISeniorStates, USZipCodesStates, unemployment, Census and BEA inputs.
